The instantaneous power in an inductor is given by  
\[
p(t) = v(t) \, i(t)
\]  
For an inductor, \( v(t) = L \frac{di}{dt} \).  
Substituting:  
\[
p(t) = L \, i(t) \, \frac{di}{dt}
\]  
So \( p(t) \) is proportional to the product of instantaneous current \( i(t) \) and the rate of change of current \( \frac{di}{dt} \).  

Final answer: (A)
